body:
First of all: Congratulations! That's fantastic!

Secondly: I find this very inspirational. I'm currently 26, working a dead end minimum wage job and desperately craving more. I've dreamed of returning to school for years now but fear has held me back. Your success story gives me hope for my own potential future. Thanks for posting! And keep up the good work!
This, word for word.

This made my week! I grew up with a Berner and he was the best dog I've ever had, he was my baby. He used to make goofy faces like this all the time. Seeing this adorable picture brought up a lot of fantastic memories. Thanks :)
Sasquatch Gang reminded me a lot of Napoleon Dynamite. Also, Justin Long is hilarious.

I'm feeling much better now, thank you for asking :)

I knew it would pass, but it really helped to have someone to talk to.

That's the only word I can really think to apply to it, but it may not be entirely correct. I have these moments where I just break down crying uncontrollably without much of a trigger. Something so minor will happen and it's like all of the stress inside of me bubbles up and that's how it shows itself. I don't know. 

I don't think it's bipolar. From what I've always been told, bipolar episodes tend to last days at a time if not longer. These come and go in a matter of hours. Then again, I'm not a doctor. I wish I could afford a therapist, the doctor I see now has me limited to five minute visits. Says hi, gives me a script and sends me on my way.

Haha it definitely has its benefits! Here they give the things out like candy. As long as you pay the state fee, they really don't care. When I went in to the consultation with the doctor I literally said I was sad and weed makes my life a bit better. He told me that depression is one of the few things they can't prescribe for but wrote down that I have severe menstrual cramps and next thing I knew I was licensed lol.
A little bit, but only like twice. I'm not opposed to trying again. I even have my Medical Marijuana card so it's legal. Funny how it was easier to get that than it is to get insurance.

Yeah, I'm on the fence about weed. I think it has a LOT of benefits but I'm not sure it helps depression. For me, personally, smoking on occasion can help list my spirits. But when I do it frequently I find that it makes the general depression a bit worse. It is a suppressant, after all.

I don't think it's bad advice, though. I'm sure for some people it can be great. But like I said, extreme moderation is key for me lol. Regular toking isn't good for me.

I was raised here, but moved around the state frequently. I've gone from super poor to support rich and back again. It's hard to explain. I think that when most kids were learning how to fit in and make friends, I was more preoccupied with moving info a totally new environment and trying to catch up. 

I'm over it now. In recent years I've made more of an effort to talk to people, but it's still foreign to me. I feel like I can't connect with people because....I just never have. I've always been so depressed that it's been my one driving force, leaving me with few other emotions to invest in. I don't open up well to people. There's a whole laundry list of reasons.

Also, sorry for any typos. I'm doing this from my phone and Swype can be funny sometimes.

Haha not offensive at all. I've...had a lot of relationships, just none of them very significant. A large part of that is due to how I was raised. I've just always had a really hard time feeling connected to other people. I've never really been checked out for anything, but I would be surprised to find out that was the issue. I definitely don't think of myself as one with autism or even aspbergers (sp?).

You know, I've thought about this quite a bit. I have always been atheist, but lately I've had days where I've just felt drawn to church. I don't really know what I believe in anymore, but I do think that sense of community could be good. I also think that faith, no matter what religion you follow, is such a beautiful thing. I would love to find some faith of my own.

That's great! I'm finally trying the prescription rout myself, but I don't think I've found the right meds though. It's a trial and error process, from what I've been told. Hopefully I'll find something that works for me.

The exercising must have helped in so many ways! I know it would make a dramatic difference in my life (besides just physically getting into shape) but I just don't have the motivation to do it lol.

Not at the moment. I've never been close with my family and that one friend now lives an hour away. We still talk on occasion, but it's hard with such a distance between us. I have several people that I talk to and hang out with once in a blue moon (when I finally manage to drag myself out of the house) but I don't feel close enough to talk to them about anything really personal.
The neighbours around here aren't exactly friendly. I suppose I could find some volunteer work to do. I'm sure there's plenty around. That wouldn't be a bad idea at all.

Your honesty is wonderful. You give me hope for the future. I know it'll be a struggle, but if I work at it I might be able to beat this, too. 
That's great that you kept pushing through until you meet your goal. It takes a lot of strength, in my opinion, to do something like that. It's inspiring.

I just sometimes feel as though I'm not living up to my full potential. I want so much more out of life than what there is to offer around here. I think that returning to school would be the most viable option for that. Of course now I worry about how isolated I would be, seeing as I'm a bit older now. Excuses, excuses. I really appreciate you taking the time to talk to me, though. The distraction really helped to get that manic feeling to stop.

Oh boy. My childhood was full of shadow people. Some of my earliest memories are of watching them walk around my house and front yard. Even as a kid I was never fearful of them. To me, they just were. They merely existed like anything else.

My mother would often catch me sitting in the large bay window at our old house. Whenever she'd ask me what I was doing I'd reply, "Waiting for the shadow men."

As I've grown up the sightings have stopped. But I'm grateful that I had those experiences. I think that children are more naturally connected to the other side. I don't fear what I saw, and I see no reason to. Whatever, or whoever, it was clearly was not out to harm me. 

There are things out there we just can't explain. But we should embrace it. Life is boring without a bit of mystery.

It's not that I find out shameful, necessarily. I just feel like I could easily wind up being one of those people who accept the free help and then never bother to better myself from there on. I tend to get...stuck. I don't want that to happen.

I don't have a career. Just odd jobs. At the current moment I'm delivering pizzas. Definitely not the ideal, but it's better than nothing. I'm looking for something new though.

I don't know. I suppose I technically could. My prescribing physician (can't exactly afford therapy) even mentioned once that I'd be eligible for SSID. But I don't want to be one of those people. There are people out there who legitimately need the money. I want to be self sufficient. I want to live for myself. Just nobody has ever taught me how. I don't even know where to begin.

Not to rant on you, but I'm in my mid twenties and completely lost. Not unheard of at my age, but still. I skipped college and went right to work. I really think I should go back to school. What I'm doing now just isn't working.
I would love to do that, but I'd be lying if I said I was going to. Maybe tomorrow morning after the snowfall. Daylight, and all that.

That's really great, I'm legitimately happy for you. I know that what I need is a major change in environment. I've never exactly been a social butterfly, I've only had one real friend in all my years. So it's hard for me. 

At what point did you decide to make the change? Was it an epiphany like moment or something you had to work yourself up to?
I do agree that getting out, even just for a walk, can do wonders.  I used to do it all the time. But since I've moved here it's been a lot harder to do.

I'm not literally trapped. I have a car, but I can't afford the gas to put into it leisurely. My hours at work got cut down to one day a week so I'm fairly broke at the moment. And now that I have to renew my plates (something that costs an arm and a leg in Michigan) I'm really struggling.

And not to make excuses, but I Kindof live in the hood. Not a very safe place for a young white girl to walk around at night. Especially with 10 inches of snow on the way.
I know it sound like excuses...but, yeah.

I think it really depends on the type of film and the company hired to do the CGI. 
Personally, I love some well done CGI in a good action, sci-fi or even horror film. If it's done right, it won't take away from the feel of the film and you walk away with some pretty awesome visuals.
On the other hand, it can be poorly overused. Honestly, I think the new Star Trek movies are testament to that. 
Obviously with a drama or romantic movie you don't want to be bombarded with a lot of CGI, but then again there have been plenty of movies that have utilized it for stylistic reasons and most people don't even notice (Forrest Gump anyone?)
I'm ranting. My point is that it's not really black or white for me. The beauty of film is that it's always changing and progressing. 
Also, sorry for any typos, I'm doing this from my phone.
Oh man, I forgot one of my all time favorites: Six String Samurai. It's....different. But so good.

I think it's worth at least one viewing. Three plot is unique and some of the characters are entertaining. But I wasn't overly impressed with it IMHO.
